claims.claim: phi-3-mini, a 3.8B model trained on 3.3T tokens, rivals Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5
claims.quote: We introduce phi-3-mini, a 3.8 billion parameter language model trained on 3.3 trillion tokens,

claims.claim: Training data is a scaled-up phi-2 dataset of heavily filtered web data and synthetic data
claims.quote: Our training dataset is a scaled-up version of the one used for phi-2, composed of heavily filtered publicly available web data and synthetic data.

claims.claim: Small enough to be deployed on a phone
claims.quote: despite being small enough to be deployed on a phone

claims.claim: Model aligned for robustness, safety and chat format
claims.quote: The model is also further aligned for robustness, safety, and chat format.

claims.claim: Parameter-scaling results with 7B and 14B models trained on 4.8T tokens
claims.quote: We also provide parameter-scaling results with a 7B, 14B models trained for 4.8T tokens

claims.claim: phi-3.5 series improves multilingual, multimodal and long-context capabilities
claims.quote: To enhance multilingual, multimodal, and long-context capabilities, we introduce three models in the phi-3.5 series:

claims.claim: phi-3.5-MoE (16x3.8B, 6.6B active) outperforms similar-scale open models
claims.quote: The phi-3.5-MoE, a 16 x 3.8B MoE model with 6.6 billion active parameters, achieves superior performance in language reasoning, math, and code tasks

claims.claim: phi-3.5-Vision 4.2B multimodal model handles single- and multi-image prompts
claims.quote: excels in reasoning tasks and is adept at handling both single-image and text prompts, as well as multi-image and text prompts

rerun.quote: All the reported numbers are produced with the exact same pipeline to ensure that the numbers are comparable.

scores_copied.quote: We just copied and pasted their published numbers since the model is not publicly available.

data_disclosure.quote: Our training data of consists of heavily filtered publicly available web data (according to the "educational level") from various open internet sources, as well as synthetic LLM-generated data.

tokens_disclosed.quote: We trained using bfloat16 for a total of 3.3T tokens.

coding.note: Claims were taken only from the abstract and introduction. The 'novel blocksparse attention' (section 2) is not listed as a claim because it does not appear in the abstract or introduction, and the paper has no ablation for it. The main text-model table was re-evaluated with the same pipeline, so rerun=YES. scores_copied=MIXED because the vision table copies published scores for MM1. The data_disclosure quote on page 3 uses straight quotes, but the source has curly quotes, so it may fail the verbatim check. The red-teaming was done by an internal Microsoft team, so third_party=NO.
